title: Conclusions & evaluations
examples: How do I know if my results are reliable enough?
What makes a conclusion strong in a science report?
Can I suggest improvements even if the experiment was successful?

explain.say: Today we learn how to evaluate your science experiment results. You must look closely at your collected data. This helps you draw strong conclusions.
First we look for trends in the data you collected. A trend shows a clear pattern or relationship. For example, as temperature increases, the resistance usually increases.
Next we must spot any anomalies in your measurements. An anomaly is a point that does not fit the expected pattern. You should investigate why this unusual point occurred.
Finally we suggest improvements for future work. This shows you know the method's weaknesses. You could suggest using more precise equipment next time.

faq.q: What is the difference between a trend and an anomaly?
faq.a: A trend is a general pattern across most of your data points. An anomaly is a single data point that breaks that established pattern.
asks: What is a pattern in my graph?
How do I spot an outlier?

faq.q: Should I always suggest an improvement?
faq.a: Yes, suggesting improvements is part of a good evaluation. It shows you understand the limitations of your method.
asks: Do I have to suggest something?
Is it bad if I cannot improve the method?

faq.q: How do I describe a trend in words?
faq.a: You can describe it by stating the relationship clearly. For example, 'the rate increased proportionally with the force applied.'
asks: How do I write about a trend?
What words should I use for a trend?

faq.q: If I find an anomaly, should I throw the data point away?
faq.a: Do not just remove it without explanation. You must explain why it might be an anomaly, perhaps due to human error.
asks: What if an anomaly is due to equipment error?

faq.q: What does it mean to evaluate the method?
faq.a: It means critically judging how well your experiment was set up. You look at what worked and what did not work well.
asks: How do I judge my own experiment?

facts: A trend describes a consistent pattern seen across multiple data points.
An anomaly is a data point that deviates significantly from the expected trend.
Evaluating a method requires considering sources of error and limitations.
Suggesting improvements shows critical thinking about experimental design.

quiz.say: If you plot time versus distance, and the points form a straight line going up, what have you observed?
quiz.why: A straight line indicates a constant rate of change, which is a clear trend.

wrong.0: This means one variable decreases as the other increases, which is not what a straight line up shows.
wrong.1: A straight line shows a very clear and strong relationship between the variables.
wrong.3: An anomaly is a single point that breaks the pattern, not the pattern itself.

quiz.say: Your measured voltage suddenly drops much lower than expected for a given resistance. This point is best described as:
quiz.why: An anomaly is defined as a measurement that does not fit the established pattern or trend.

wrong.0: A trend describes the general pattern, not a single unexpected point.
wrong.1: A conclusion is a final statement, not a specific piece of raw data.
wrong.2: Improvements are suggestions for the future, not measurements from the past.

quiz.say: To improve the accuracy of measuring mass, you could use:

options.show: A digital balance with higher precision
options.say: A digital balance with higher precision

quiz.why: Using more precise equipment directly addresses the limitation of measurement accuracy.

wrong.1: Sample size relates more to repeating measurements, not the precision of one reading.
wrong.2: Changing units does not fix the inherent precision limit of the instrument itself.
wrong.3: Time period is irrelevant when the limitation is the accuracy of the balance reading.
